survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports descriptive PISA 2022 results for Peru (and comparisons to OECD averages and selected countries) rather than estimating a student-level predictive model. PISA uses a complex sampling design with stratification and clustering at school and student levels; analysts working with the PISA microdata typically apply the provided sampling weights to obtain population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify which weight variables (e.g., student/sampling weights) or replicate-weight procedures were used, so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the text. For any re-analysis using PISA 2022 microdata, users should apply the official PISA sampling weights and, where available, replicate weights to correctly quantify uncertainty (confidence intervals) under the complex design.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Peru performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). PISA 2022 uses two two-hour subject tests with rotated booklets so that different students receive different item sets, alongside student and school questionnaires. The factsheet reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic divides (international ESCS quintiles) and gender differences. It also highlights COVID-related learning experiences, with a caution that only 56% of students reached the final questionnaire section. No machine-learning models are trained or evaluated in this document; therefore, there are no predictive metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) to extract, and causal interpretations are not part of the reported analysis.
